decisions.decision: Phase 2 wrapper HOVER strategy: subprocess _run_hover.py wrapping translate_for_target_real, NOT in-process import
decisions.rationale: Sidesteps dual-rclpy-Node coupling. Matches existing primitive-orchestration pattern (translate_object.py:1085 -> insertion subprocess). Easy to flip to in-process if Phase 5/6 surfaces a need.

decisions.decision: Phase 2 STEP-BACK gate: --step-back {prompt,signal,auto} runtime flag, default 'prompt' (stdin Y/N)
decisions.rationale: Prompt is safest (operator must explicitly confirm). Signal mode (SIGUSR1 trigger) supports headless dispatcher use. Auto mode is for repeated-attempt sessions with operator already-stepped-back.

decisions.decision: Phase 2 wrapper |Fz| capped at 5 N unless --override-fz-cap explicit
decisions.rationale: CONVENTIONS: gear/part/fixture damage limit. Cap is enforced in _start_force_mode() before SetForceMode RPC.

decisions.decision: Phase 2 known limitation: target_x/y/z columns reference HOVER pose, not the actual hole world coords
decisions.rationale: Hole world coords are a Phase 5 deliverable (per-object YAML wires offsets). Wrapper now logs a loud WARN line at HOVER completion so the limitation surfaces in every episode's stdout. CSV is schema-compliant; dx/dy/dz won't be physically meaningful for termination derivation until Phase 5.
